observed_behavior: The sealed Candidate loader follows a Windows junction within the registry ancestor chain when the leaf candidate file itself is ordinary.
expected_behavior: Every path component from canonical registry root through the Candidate leaf rejects symlinks, junctions and reparse points and the leaf is read with stable no-follow semantics.
impact: Review and delivery snapshots can consume Candidate bytes outside the canonical registry, breaking sealed identity and promotion trust boundaries.

reproduction.symptom_oracle: Ancestor and leaf redirects plus read-time swaps must return a stable Candidate error; an ordinary canonical registry path remains accepted.
steps: Create an isolated Windows registry with repos/<repo_id> as a real junction to an external candidate tree.
Keep the candidate.json leaf an ordinary file and call _candidate_path.
Compare the accepted loader result with the shared component-walk _redirected result.
reproduction.sample: The independent Reviewer and main-agent probes each reproduced acceptance once; the shared redirect detector returned true for the same candidate path.

root_cause.summary: default_registry_root checks only the registry root and _candidate_path checks only the leaf. No component-walk or stable no-follow read protects nested registry ancestors, so a repos/<repo_id> junction is transparently followed.

next_action: Implementation executor invalidates WP-002 and downstream WPs, adds real junction, leaf redirect and swap regression reds, then applies an equivalent component-safe stable Candidate read and reruns Windows, Linux and fresh review.
